archetype.name: Rebuilding (young core, early)
archetype.definition: A team still building around its young forwards, with Bedard, Nazar, Frondell, Kantserov, Levshunov and Rinzel carrying big roles, that is not yet close to competing and is losing the run of play most nights.

report.headline: Bottom of the league and earning it: outshot, outchanced and outgoaltended nightly.
report.take:
Chicago is 5-13-2 and the record is honest. The Blackhawks rank last in Goal Diff / GP at -1.85. They are 32nd in scoring and 31st in goals allowed, and their Pts vs Goal Diff of 0.4 sits right in the middle of the league. Close games and overtime haven't been unkind to them. They simply lose by a lot. The pace line says the same thing in a harsher way: 21 wins and 49 standings points over 82 games, down from the 72 points of last season.

The cause is territorial. At 5-on-5 Chicago owns 40.9% of the expected goals (31st) and 44% of the shot attempts (30th). It puts 22.9 shots on goal a game against a league average of 27.4 and gives up 30. That gap shows up across the roster. Every forward and defenseman listed has an xGF % below .500. Nazar's .48 is the best of the regulars, and the top pair of Vlasic and Levshunov sits around .39 while playing more than 20 minutes a night. Both skater groups grade F. The defense also gives up more than expected to every position: forwards score 1.48 points a game above their norms against Chicago, 31st in the league.

The numbers hide some bad luck, but not enough to change the picture. The 5-on-5 PDO is 96.4 and the all-situations PDO of 97.4 ranks 31st. The skaters shoot 10% against a league 11.4%, and the goalies stop .873 against .892. Some of that will drift back toward normal. But the expected-goals share has slid each year, from .431 to .424 to .409 now, so the process is getting worse, not better. The goaltending that saved this team last year, at 7.5 GSAx, has flipped to -10.3. Arvid Soderblom accounts for -6.1 of it in only four starts.

The real hope is Connor Bedard. He has 17 points in 14 games, with a 13.0 Game Score that leads the team by a wide margin and six PP Points, and he plays 20.72 minutes a night. Chicago has played 20 games and he has dressed for 14 of them, and the offense around him is thin. Patrick Kane has one goal on 32 shots, and the power play converts at 14.3% (30th). Expect a modest climb from the bottom as the save percentage normalizes. Expect no climb out of the bottom tier until the 5-on-5 share moves.

strengths.title: Bedard is a genuine top-line engine
strengths.body: Bedard has 17 points in 14 games and a 13.0 Game Score, which no other Blackhawk approaches, and he logs a team-high 20.72 minutes among the forwards. Six of his points have come on a power play that otherwise barely functions. That production is real talent, not a hot streak, but on a team with a 41% expected-goals share it can only blunt the losses.

strengths.title: Young finishers are scoring anyway
strengths.body: Kantserov has 9 goals and Nazar has 8, so the kids are converting what little the team generates. Nazar's .48 xGF % is the best on-ice share among the regulars, which suggests his line can hold its own. Kantserov's nine goals on 32 shots and his .358 xGF % look more like finishing luck that will cool.

strengths.title: Penalty kill holds at league level
strengths.body: The PK runs at 78.1%, 15th and slightly above the league average of 77.4%. Last year it killed 83.6%, so this is a step back but still a functional unit. It is the one phase of the game where Chicago isn't giving ground every night.

concerns.title: Buried at 5-on-5, and getting worse
concerns.body: Chicago's 40.9% expected-goals share and 44% Corsi both sit at the bottom of the league. It is outshot 30 to 22.9 a game. The xGF % has fallen from .424 last season, so this is a structural problem that is deepening, and it is the main reason the goal differential is last.

concerns.title: Goaltending has turned from asset to liability
concerns.body: Team GSAx sits at -10.3 (30th) after +7.5 last season, and the save % of .873 ranks 28th. Knight is merely below par at .882 and -2.3. Soderblom's .842 and -6.1 over four starts have done outsized damage. Some recovery is likely, but behind this shot volume even average goaltending leaves plenty of goals against.

concerns.title: Power play can't cash
concerns.body: At 14.3% the PP is 30th, well under the league's 22.2%. Bedard is the only skater with more than three PP Points, and Kane has one goal on 32 shots. On a team this starved for 5-on-5 offense, a dead power play removes the easiest path to goals.

trend.note: October was poor at 3.69 goals allowed a game, and November has been worse at 5.00, including a 9-2 loss at Carolina. The last five games allowed 5.0 a game, 0.85 above the season rate, while the points percentage has stayed stuck at .300.

weekAhead.headline: Four sub-.500 opponents, ending with the league's worst team
weekAhead.body:
This is as soft a week as Chicago will see. Toronto, Columbus, Calgary and Vancouver all sit 25th or lower on the site. The two home games are tougher than the records suggest. Toronto's 8-12-2 comes with a -4.3 Pts vs Goal Diff, 31st, so the Leafs have been unlucky, and they carry a PP at 26.7% and a PK at 85.7%, both top-seven units. Columbus has the league's worst shooting % at .088 and the 30th-ranked offense, the kind of opponent that can let Knight post a respectable night.

The western swing closes on consecutive days. Calgary's 9-11-1 is propped up by a 3.1 Pts vs Goal Diff (2nd), and its offense ranks 29th, so this is a winnable game, though the Flames' 27.1% PP punishes penalties. Vancouver is the best chance on the schedule. The Canucks rank 32nd in xGF %, save %, PK % and GSAx, and they allow forwards more points above expectation than anyone. Even so, Chicago's own process numbers barely differ from Vancouver's, so splitting the week would count as a good outcome.

keyMatchups.title: Chicago's power play vs Vancouver's kill
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver kills only 62% of its penalties, last in the league, and its goalies stop .862 in all situations, also last. Chicago's 14.3% power play needs exactly this kind of opponent to break out. If Bedard's unit can't score here, the PP problem goes deeper than the opposition.

keyMatchups.title: Wingers against a sieve
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver allows wingers 1.55 points a game above their expected output, 32nd in the league. That sets up well for Kantserov, Bertuzzi and Kane. Kane in particular, with one goal on 32 shots, is due for the kind of game where the puck finally goes in.

keyMatchups.title: Discipline against TOR and CGY
keyMatchups.body: Toronto's PP at 26.7% (6th) and Calgary's at 27.1% (5th) are the most dangerous weapons Chicago faces this week. The Blackhawks' kill is middle-of-the-pack at 78.1%. Staying out of the box is the clearest way to keep both games close.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in Vancouver on the back end of the consecutive-day trip. A Soderblom start (.842, -6.1 GSAx) could squander the easiest game on the schedule.

restOfSeason.body:
The bad-luck portion of Chicago's season is real but small. An all-situations PDO of 97.4 and a goalie save % far below the league should drift upward, and Knight was a positive goaltender on this franchise last year. That alone should lift the team off its 49-point pace. What won't change on its own is a 40.9% expected-goals share and a shot deficit near the bottom of the league, carried by two F-graded skater groups. My expectation is a finish of 56 to 66 standings points, an improvement on the current pace but likely short of last season's 72.

The ceiling depends on Bedard staying in the lineup and on the young defense learning to get the puck out. The floor depends on goaltending. If Soderblom keeps getting starts at his current level, goals against stay near four a game. If Knight absorbs the bulk of the starts and settles near average, something closer to 3.5 is realistic. Either way, this projects as a bottom-three finish and another high draft pick.
swingFactors: Knight's save % and how many starts Soderblom gets
Bedard's availability and the power play's conversion
Any movement in the 5-on-5 expected-goals share

confidence.note: 20 games is a modest sample, but the shot and chance shares match two prior bottom-three seasons.
